task.description: Verify the GBL-137 forward-fix for ISS-0620/GH-573 (BLOCKER) against real PostgreSQL. Confirm zig build, migrate idempotency against both known-affected databases (bpm_test, bpm_dev), and zig build test-env-verify all pass, with correct environment configuration (this workspace's shell has a pre-existing, unrelated ~/.bashrc misconfiguration -- see below).

result.summary: GitHub Actions status: operational (checked). zig build: PASS (exit 0). zig build migrate: genuine no-op ('No new migrations to apply') against BOTH bpm_test (port 5453) and bpm_dev (port 5452) -- GBL-137 confirmed already applied and idempotent in both. IMPORTANT ENVIRONMENT FINDING (unrelated to this fix, worth recording): this workspace's shell has a pre-existing ~/.bashrc line hardcoding BPM_TEST_DB_URL to port 5434 -- the SIBLING workspace's (r-co-1) test DB, not this workspace's own port 5453 (which .env correctly specifies). This caused zig build test-env-verify to initially report UNHEALTHY (C1: wrong container port; C4: schema-baseline mismatch against the wrong, unrelated database) -- NOT a real defect in GBL-137. Confirmed by re-running with BPM_TEST_DB_URL explicitly overridden inline to port 5453: verify_test_env reports HEALTHY, 10/10 checks passed, including C4 schema baseline (112/112 migrations match ledger, confirming GBL-137 is correctly recorded and applied). This is a session-level shell misconfiguration outside this repository -- not fixed here (editing the user's personal ~/.bashrc is out of scope for this fix), but noted for future sessions. lint_dual_schema_table_names.py: reports 21 BLOCKER duplicate-table findings against bpm_test -- independently confirmed these are the SAME already-filed, already-queued ISS-0623/GH-580 finding (bpm_test's unrelated tenant_default reprovisioning event resurrecting previously-dropped GLOBAL_REGISTRY tables), NOT the 4 tables this fix targets (entity_definitions/entity_type_instances/entity_record_latest/artifact_activation_groups do not appear in this finding's list) and NOT caused by GBL-137. This finding is out of scope for GH-573 and does not block this fix's release -- ISS-0623/GH-580 is already queued for its own future run.
result.next_action: Route to RELEASE-VALIDATOR (Step 5) -- required given BLOCKER severity, per WF-03 pipeline table.
